attributes.title: Level 3

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you check the sequence of blocks within the [list add value to end] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What should the project ask the user when the Player sprite overlaps with a blue button tile?


Solution: 

The (ask for string) value block should contain the (join) block, which should join the string “Type a(n)” and the (get and remove first value from list) block.
steps.instructions:
When the Player sprite overlaps with each blue button tile, the project only asks for user input for the category, “feeling”. 


Fix the bugs in the code so that when the Player sprite overlaps with a blue button tile, the project asks for user input for each of the four categories, by getting and removing the first value from the list.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ What tile does the conditional check for in the (array of all tile locations) block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Will the array of all gray path tiles ever be equal to zero? Which tile should be selected instead?


Solution: 

The tile in the (array of all tile locations) block should be changed from a gray path tile, to a blue button tile.
steps.instructions:
After the Player sprite has overlapped with each of the four blue button tiles, a dialog box does not appear.


Fix the bugs in the code so that a dialog box that says, “Hello world! I have a story to tell you!”, appears once all of the button tiles have been changed to path tiles.

steps.hints: ❓ What is the name of the array that contains the user input variables?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which array should the (join) block pull values from, in order to complete the sentence with user input?


Solution: 

The list in each of the (get value at index) value blocks should be changed from [text list] to [userResponseList].
steps.instructions:
When the completed story is read, the dialog box reads, “One day, undefined was feeling undefined.”


Fix the bugs in the code so that the dialog box retrieves the user inputted variables from the correct array and replaces undefined with the user’s responses.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Orange Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about user input, variables, and arrays. A variable stores one piece of information, while an array stores multiple pieces of information, of the same data type, in an ordered list. Variables and arrays can take in information while they are being created, while the program is running, and from user input. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Making a List
